fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. Wisdom does the opposite of whispering in a back room. She "…calls out in the street…" and "…lifts her voice in the square…" and she makes her speech "…at the city gates…" (Proverbs 1:20-21). Those are out in the open, not in a quiet room.

Good guess, but the text doesn't name priests or kings here. Wisdom turns to "scoffers" and "fools" right after the simple ones (Proverbs 1:22). The scoffers delight in their scorn, and the fools hate knowledge. Those are the ones she names.

Right on the money, friend! Wisdom asks, "How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways?" (Proverbs 1:22). Then she says they "…refused my call…" and "…neglected all my counsel…" (Proverbs 1:24-25). I think that's why she asks. Her question comes after they've turned her down.

Not quite, friend. The text never says she just arrived. It says she "…calls out in the street…" (Proverbs 1:20). Her question, "How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways?" (Proverbs 1:22), is about what the simple ones are doing. Then she says they "…refused my call…" (Proverbs 1:24).

Ha! I wish she were just checking her watch, baker. But "How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways?" (Proverbs 1:22) isn't about a clock. It's aimed at the simple ones and their simple ways. Then she says they "…refused my call…" (Proverbs 1:24).

That's right, friend, and what a way to end! Wisdom finishes with, "But whoever listens to me will dwell in safety, secure from the fear of evil." (Proverbs 1:33). After all those hard words, she ends on a promise. Whoever listens gets safety. I love that she lands there.
